name: Acute Limb Ischaemia

matching.reasoningTemplate: Sudden severe limb pain in a patient with an embolic source (atrial fibrillation) or peripheral arterial disease indicates acute limb ischaemia — a time-critical vascular emergency (the 6 Ps).

redFlags: Time-critical — irreversible tissue loss within ~6 h; pain, pallor, pulselessness, paraesthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia
Paralysis/anaesthesia (Rutherford IIb→III) → immediate revascularisation or the limb is lost
Systemic anticoagulate immediately unless contraindicated; urgent vascular referral

investigations.test: Handheld Doppler of distal pulses + ankle pressures
Urgent CT/MR/catheter angiography to localise occlusion

references: Harrison 22e — Vascular Diseases of the Extremities
provenanceNote: Recall Tier-4 (Group B) new diagnosable entity. AI-drafted; PENDING clinician sign-off. Uses only existing governed finding keys (no vocabulary change).

algorithms.title: Acute Limb Ischaemia: Diagnostic & Clinical Decision Pathway

steps.action: Evaluate acute presentation and core clinical features of Acute Limb Ischaemia.
Screen for high-risk signs: Time-critical - irreversible tissue loss within ~6 h; pain, pallor, pulselessness, paraesthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia
Targeted workup: Handheld Doppler of distal pulses + ankle pressures, Urgent CT/MR/catheter angiography to localise occlusion, ECG (atrial fibrillation), FBC, coagulation, group-and-save
Apply evidence-based criteria to classify disease severity and organ dysfunction.
Initiate guideline-directed medical therapy and monitor clinical progress.
